name: abs
description: The `abs()` function returns the non‑negative magnitude of its argument, whether that argument is an integer, a float, a complex number (returning its modulus), or any object that defines an `__abs__` method.

name: aiter
description: The aiter() function returns an asynchronous iterator by invoking the __aiter__() method of an asynchronous iterable, providing a direct way to obtain an async iterator without supporting a two‑argument form.

name: all
description: The `all()` function checks an iterable and returns True only if every element evaluates as true (or if the iterable is empty), otherwise it returns False.

name: anext
description: `anext()` asynchronously retrieves the next element from an async iterator (optionally returning a default value if the iterator is exhausted) by awaiting its `__anext__()` method.

name: any
description: The any() function iterates over an iterable and returns True if it encounters at least one truthy element, otherwise it returns False (including when the iterable is empty).

name: ascii
description: The ascii() function returns a printable string representation of an object like repr(), but with all non‑ASCII characters escaped using \x, \u, or \U sequences.

name: bin
description: The bin() function converts an integer (or any object defining __index__) into its binary string representation, optionally prefixed with “0b”.

name: bool
description: The bool() function converts a given value to its Boolean truth value, returning True for any object that is truthy and False for falsey values (including when no argument is provided).

name: breakpoint
description: The `breakpoint()` function provides a single-call entry point that invokes `sys.breakpointhook()` (defaulting to `pdb.set_trace()`) to drop execution into a debugger, allowing customization via the `PYTHONBREAKPOINT` environment variable or by overriding the hook.

name: bytearray
description: The `bytearray()` function creates a mutable sequence of bytes, optionally initialized from a string (with encoding), a specified size of zero‑filled bytes, a buffer, or an iterable of integers in the 0‑255 range, or returns an empty byte array if no argument is given.

name: bytes
description: The `bytes()` function creates an immutable sequence of 0‑255 integer values (a bytes object), interpreting its arguments like `bytearray()` and supporting the same non‑mutating methods, indexing, and slicing.

name: callable
description: It checks whether a given object can be invoked like a function, returning True if the object is callable (including classes and objects with a __call__ method) and False otherwise.

name: chr
description: The chr() function converts an integer Unicode code point (0‑0x10FFFF) into the corresponding one‑character string, raising ValueError for out‑of‑range values.

name: classmethod
description: classmethod() decorates a function so it receives the owning class as its first argument, allowing the method to be called on the class or any instance while behaving like a regular method bound to the class.

name: compile

signatures.raw_signature: compile(source, filename, mode, flags=0, dont_inherit=False, optimize=-1)

description: The compile() function transforms a source string, byte string, or AST object into a code object (or AST) that can be executed by exec() or eval(), allowing specification of filename, compilation mode, flags, inheritance behavior, and optimization level.

name: complex
description: The `complex()` function converts a string or numeric input (or separate real and imaginary parts) into a Python complex number, handling various formats and delegating to an object's `__complex__`, `__float__`, or `__index__` methods when needed.

name: delattr
description: delattr() removes a specified attribute from an object by name, functioning like the statement del object.attribute.

name: dict
description: The dict() function constructs and returns a new dictionary object, optionally initializing it from mappings, keyword arguments, or iterable key‑value pairs.

name: dir
description: The dir() function returns a sorted list of the names of attributes available in the current local scope when called without arguments, or the accessible attributes of a given object (using its __dir__ method if present, otherwise gathering from its __dict__, type, and inheritance hierarchy).

name: divmod
description: The divmod() function takes two numbers and returns a tuple containing their integer quotient and remainder, matching the behavior of (a // b, a % b) for integers and providing a floor‑based quotient with a remainder that satisfies the usual division identity for floats.

name: enumerate
description: The enumerate() function creates an iterator that yields pairs of an index (starting from a specified start value, default 0) and each element from a given iterable.

name: eval
description: The eval() function parses and evaluates a given Python expression (or compiled code object) using optional global and local namespace mappings and returns the result, while warning that executing untrusted code is insecure.

name: exec
description: exec() dynamically executes a given string or code object as Python statements within optional global and local namespaces, returning None.

name: filter
description: The filter() function creates an iterator that yields each element from the given iterable for which the provided function returns True, or, if the function is None, yields only the elements that are truthy.

name: float
description: float() converts a given numeric value or properly formatted string—including optional signs, whitespace, exponent, “inf”, or “nan”—into a Python floating‑point number, returning 0.0 when called without an argument and raising OverflowError for values outside the float range.

name: format
description: The `format()` function returns a string representation of a value according to a given format specification by invoking the value’s type-specific `__format__` method, defaulting to `str(value)` when the specification is empty.

name: frozenset
description: The frozenset() function creates an immutable set object, optionally populated with elements from a given iterable.

name: getattr
description: `getattr()` returns the value of a specified attribute from an object, optionally providing a default value instead of raising an AttributeError when the attribute does not exist.

name: globals
description: `globals()` returns the dictionary representing the current module’s global symbol table, providing access to all globally defined names at the point where the function is called.

name: hasattr
description: The `hasattr()` function checks whether a given object possesses an attribute with a specified name, returning True if it exists and False otherwise.

name: hash
description: The Python `hash()` function returns an integer hash value for an object, enabling fast key comparisons in dictionaries and ensuring that numerically equal values share the same hash, with results truncated to the machine’s word size.

name: help
description: The built‑in help() function launches Python’s interactive documentation system, displaying a help page for the interpreter, a named object, or any object passed as an argument.

name: hex
description: The hex() function returns a string representing an integer’s value in lowercase hexadecimal notation prefixed with “0x”, raising an error for non‑int objects unless they implement __index__().

name: id
description: The `id()` function returns a unique integer representing an object's identity, which remains constant for the object's lifetime (often its memory address in CPython).

name: input
description: The `input()` function optionally displays a prompt, reads a line from standard input, strips the trailing newline, returns it as a string, and raises EOFError if end‑of‑file is encountered.

name: int
description: int() creates an integer from a numeric value, a string (optionally with a specified base), or returns 0 when called without arguments, using __int__ or __index__ methods if present.

name: isinstance
description: `isinstance()` returns True when a given object is an instance of a specified type (or any type in a tuple or Union) and False otherwise, raising TypeError only if the type argument is invalid.

name: issubclass
description: issubclass() returns True if the given class is a direct, indirect, virtual subclass of the specified class or any class within a tuple or Union Type, treating a class as a subclass of itself, otherwise it raises a TypeError.

name: iter
description: The iter() function creates an iterator either from an iterable object (or sequence) when called with one argument or from a callable that repeatedly produces values until a specified sentinel value is returned, at which point iteration stops.

name: len
description: The len() function returns the number of elements in a sequence or collection, raising OverflowError if the length exceeds sys.maxsize.

name: list
description: The list() callable constructs a new mutable sequence (list) from an iterable or creates an empty list when called without arguments.

name: locals
description: locals() returns a mapping of the current local symbol table, reflecting variable names and their bound objects, and in optimized scopes provides a snapshot dictionary that isn’t written back to actual locals.

name: map
description: The `map()` function returns an iterator that applies a given function to each element of one or more iterables in parallel, yielding the results and optionally raising a ValueError if any iterable is exhausted before the others when `strict=True`.

name: max
description: The max() function returns the greatest element from a single iterable or the greatest of multiple provided arguments, optionally using a key function for ordering and a default value for empty iterables.

name: memoryview
description: memoryview() creates a lightweight object that provides a read‑only or writable view of an existing object's binary data without copying it, allowing direct byte‑wise access and manipulation.

name: min
description: The `min()` function returns the smallest element from an iterable or the smallest of given arguments, optionally using a key function for ordering and a default value to return when the iterable is empty.

name: next
description: The `next()` function fetches the upcoming element from an iterator by invoking its `__next__()` method, returning a provided default value if the iterator is exhausted, otherwise raising `StopIteration`.

name: object
description: The `object()` function creates a new, featureless base‑class instance that serves as the ultimate parent of all Python classes and cannot be given arguments or have arbitrary attributes added.

name: oct
description: The oct() function takes an integer (or any object with an __index__ method) and returns its octal representation as a string prefixed with “0o”.

name: open

signatures.raw_signature: open(file, mode=r, buffering=-1, encoding=None, errors=None, newline=None, closefd=True, opener=None)

description: The built‑in `open()` function opens a file (or file descriptor) with a specified mode, encoding, buffering, and other options, returning a corresponding file object for reading, writing, or both, and raises an OSError if the operation fails.

name: ord
description: The ord() function returns the integer Unicode code point of a single-character string or the numeric byte value of a one‑byte bytes or bytearray object.

name: pow
description: The pow() function computes base raised to the exponent, optionally performing modular exponentiation efficiently when a third mod argument is provided, handling type coercion, negative exponents, and returning floats, complex numbers, or modular inverses as appropriate.

name: print
description: The print() function converts given objects to strings, writes them to a text stream (defaulting to sys.stdout) separated by a specified separator and terminated by a specified end string, optionally flushing the stream.

name: property
description: `property()` creates a descriptor that links attribute access, assignment, and deletion on a class to custom getter, setter, and deleter functions, optionally providing a docstring, enabling managed or read‑only attributes.

name: getter
description: The `getter()` function retrieves and returns a specific value or object from a data source, encapsulating the access logic for reuse.

name: setter
description: The `setter()` function assigns a given value to a specified attribute or key within an object, dictionary, or similar data structure, optionally performing validation or transformation before storing the value.

name: deleter
description: The `deleter()` method creates a new property object identical to the original but with its delete accessor (`fdel`) replaced by the decorated function, enabling custom deletion behavior for the property.

name: __name__
description: `__name__` is a special attribute that holds the identifier of a module, class, or function, allowing the code to determine its own name (e.g., to distinguish between being run as a script or imported) and can be modified at runtime.

name: range
description: The `range()` function generates an immutable sequence of evenly spaced integers defined by start, stop, and step parameters, allowing efficient iteration and indexing without storing all values in memory.

name: repr
description: repr() returns a printable string representation of an object, typically one that can be passed to eval() to recreate the object, or a descriptive placeholder if that is not possible.

name: reversed
description: The reversed() function returns an iterator that yields the elements of a sequence or any object with a __reversed__() method in the opposite order from their original arrangement.

name: round
description: The `round()` function returns a number rounded to a specified number of decimal places (or to the nearest integer if no precision is given), using “bankers rounding” where ties are rounded to the nearest even value.

name: set
description: The set() function creates and returns a new mutable set object, optionally initializing it with elements drawn from a given iterable.

name: setattr
description: setattr(obj, name, value) dynamically assigns the given value to the specified attribute (or creates it) on the object, effectively performing the equivalent of the dot‑notation assignment obj.name = value.

name: slice
description: The `slice()` function creates a slice object that encodes the start, stop, and step indices for slicing operations, allowing those indices to be stored, reused, and (as of Python 3.12) hashed.

name: start
description: The start() function initializes the class’s read‑only attributes using the supplied arguments or their defaults, enabling NumPy and other third‑party packages to access those values.

name: sorted
description: The `sorted()` function returns a new list containing the elements of an iterable ordered according to optional key and reverse parameters, while preserving the original order of equal items (stable sort).

name: staticmethod
description: staticmethod() converts a regular function into a class‑level method that receives no implicit instance or class argument, allowing it to be called on the class or its instances like a plain function.

name: str
description: The built-in `str()` function converts any given object into its string representation.

name: sum
description: The built‑in `sum()` function adds a start value to all numeric items of an iterable, processing them left‑to‑right, and returns the total.

name: super
description: super() returns a proxy that searches the method‑resolution‑order after a specified class (or the current class when called without arguments) to delegate attribute or method lookups to the next parent or sibling class, enabling overridden methods to be accessed and supporting cooperative multiple inheritance.

name: tuple
description: The tuple() function converts an iterable (or no argument) into an immutable sequence object of type tuple.

name: type
description: The `type()` built‑in returns an object’s type when called with one argument, and when given three arguments (name, bases, dict) dynamically creates a new class object.

name: vars
description: The `vars()` function returns an object's attribute dictionary (its `__dict__`) or, when called without arguments, behaves like `locals()` to provide the current local symbol table.

name: zip
description: zip() creates a lazy iterator that aggregates elements from multiple iterables into tuples, pairing the i‑th items together (stopping at the shortest iterable unless strict=True is used).

name: __import__
description: The built‑in __import__() function is the low‑level mechanism invoked by the import statement to locate and load a module (or package) using optional globals, locals, from‑list and level arguments, though direct use is discouraged in favor of importlib.import_module().
